match.reason: The bank point covers the broad shift from Britain and Europe to Asia at Year 12 depth, but it lacks the brief's Year 9 detail: wool and wheat as the 1950s export leaders, Japan's historical lead, and the shift to minerals and energy, which would need new content rather than small changes.

draft.title: How Australia's trade has changed
card: In the 1950s, Britain was Australia's main trading partner. Wool and wheat led Australia's exports.
Later, Japan took over as the main partner. It bought large amounts of Australian minerals and energy, such as iron ore and coal.
Today, Asia buys most of Australia's exports, and China is the largest buyer. Minerals and energy lead the exports.
So both the main partner and the main exports have changed over time. Farm products led first, and then minerals and energy.
draft.remember: Australia's trade moved from Britain, wool and wheat to Asia, minerals and energy.

a.q: Which pair best describes Australia's main trading partner and leading exports in the 1950s?
opts: Britain, with wool and wheat
Japan, with wool and wheat
Britain, with iron ore and coal
China, with iron ore and coal
a.why: In the 1950s Britain was the main partner and wool and wheat led exports. Japan, iron ore and coal came later, when minerals and energy became the leading exports.
a.clue: Think of the earliest period on the card.

b.q: Ben says Australia's trade in the 1950s was much the same as today. Which fact shows he is wrong?
opts: Today minerals and energy lead exports, not wool and wheat
Today Australia sells goods to other countries
Today Australia trades with more than one country
Today Australia sells some farm products overseas
b.why: The main exports have changed from wool and wheat to minerals and energy, so the two periods differ. The other options are true now, but they were also true in the 1950s, so they do not show a change.
b.clue: Find something that was different in the 1950s, not something shared.

b.best: Today minerals and energy lead exports, not wool and wheat

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is clearly the longest, and it is the only one that names specific products and contrasts two periods. The other three are short, generic statements, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
